ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: Who Is the Author of AI-generated Art?

fullPassage:
Who Is the Author of AI-generated Art?

Artists usually sign their works of art to show authorship. But what about AI art? Who actually creates the work: the AI or the human using it? A major concern related to authorship is the copyright of AI-generated art. More and more companies, developers, and artists ask for legal protection of the artworks created by AI programs that they developed or used. Since current copyright law applies to humans, not machines, the "author" should be the person who arranged the creation of an AI-generated artwork. However, it is not always clear who undertook the arrangements. It could, for example, be the people who organized or funded the project, did the coding or "teaching" of the AI, or input a prompt.

Could an AI machine itself ever be considered an author with legal rights? It seems unlikely, but who knows how this question will be regarded in the future?

questions.passage: Artists usually sign their works of art to show (A)[authorship / ownership]. But what about AI art? Who actually creates the work: the AI or the human using it? A major (B)[concern / confidence] related to authorship is the copyright of AI-generated art. More and more companies, developers, and artists ask for (C)[legal / illegal] protection of the artworks created by AI programs.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 예술가들은 저작권을 보여주기 위해 서명한다. 저작권에 대한 주요 우려. 법적 보호를 요구한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① authorship — concern — legal
❌ ② ownership — concern — illegal
❌ ③ authorship — confidence — illegal
❌ ④ ownership — confidence — legal
✅ (A) authorship: 서명으로 '저작권/저자임'을 보여줌. ownership(소유권)도 가능하나 원문은 authorship. ✅ (B) concern: '우려/관심사'. confidence(자신감)는 문맥 불일치. ✅ (C) legal: '법적' 보호. illegal(불법적)은 반대.
det.tip: authorship(저작권/저자 지위) vs ownership(소유권). legal(합법적) ↔ illegal(불법적).

questions.passage: A major concern related to authorship is the copyright of AI-generated art. More and more companies, developers, and artists ask for legal protection of the artworks created by AI programs that they developed or used. Since current copyright law (A)[applies / appeals] to humans, not machines, the "author" should be the person who (B)[arranged / avoided] the creation of an AI-generated artwork. However, it is not always (C)[clear / common] who undertook the arrangements. It could, for example, be the people who organized or funded the project, did the coding or "teaching" of the AI, or input a prompt. Could an AI machine itself ever be considered an author with legal rights?
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 현행 저작권법은 인간에게 적용된다. 저작자는 창작을 주선한 사람이어야 한다. 그러나 누가 주선했는지 항상 명확하지는 않다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① appeals — arranged — common
✅ ② applies — arranged — clear ←정답
❌ ③ applies — avoided — common
❌ ④ appeals — avoided — clear
✅ (A) applies: 법이 '적용되다'. appeals(호소하다)는 법률 맥락에서 다른 의미. ✅ (B) arranged: 창작을 '주선/준비한'. avoided(피한)는 반대. ✅ (C) clear: '명확한'. common(흔한)은 문맥 불일치.
det.tip: apply to(~에 적용되다) vs appeal to(~에 호소하다). arrange(준비/주선하다).

questions.passage: More and more companies, developers, and artists ask for legal protection of the artworks created by AI programs that they developed or used. Since current copyright law applies to humans, not machines, the "author" should be the person who arranged the creation of an AI-generated artwork. However, it is not always clear who (A)[undertook / overlooked] the arrangements. It could, for example, be the people who organized or (B)[funded / abandoned] the project, did the coding or "teaching" of the AI, or input a prompt. Could an AI machine itself ever be (C)[considered / dismissed] an author with legal rights? It seems unlikely, but who knows how this question will be regarded in the future?
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: undertook — funded — considered
det.analysis:
❌ ① overlooked — funded — dismissed
❌ ② undertook — abandoned — dismissed
✅ ④ undertook — funded — considered ←정답
❌ ④ overlooked — abandoned — considered
✅ (A) undertook: '수행하다'. overlooked(간과하다)는 반대 뉘앙스. ✅ (B) funded: '자금을 지원한'. abandoned(포기한)는 반대. ✅ (C) considered: '간주되다'. dismissed(기각되다)는 반대.
det.tip: undertake(수행하다) ↔ overlook(간과하다). fund(자금 지원) ↔ abandon(포기하다).

questions.passage: Artists usually ①<u>sign</u> their works of art to show authorship. But what about AI art? Who actually creates the work: the AI or the human using it? A major concern related to authorship is the ②<u>copyright</u> of AI-generated art. More and more companies, developers, and artists ask for legal ③<u>protection</u> of the artworks created by AI programs that they developed or used. Since current copyright law applies to humans, not machines, the "author" should be the person who ④<u>rejected</u> the creation of an AI-generated artwork.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 저자는 AI 생성 예술 작품의 창작을 주선한(arranged) 사람이어야 한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①sign(서명하다): 원문 그대로. ✅ ②copyright(저작권): 원문 그대로. ✅ ③protection(보호): 원문 그대로. ❌ ④rejected(거부한): 원문은 arranged(주선한). 창작을 '거부한' 사람이 저자가 되는 것은 논리적 모순.
det.tip: arranged(주선하다) ↔ rejected(거부하다). 창작을 주선한 사람 = 저자.

questions.passage: However, it is not always clear who ④<u>undertook</u> the arrangements. It could, for example, be the people who ②<u>organized</u> or funded the project, did the coding or "teaching" of the AI, or ③<u>input</u> a prompt. Could an AI machine itself ever be considered an author with ①<u>physical</u> rights?
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: AI 기계가 법적(legal) 권리를 가진 저자로 간주될 수 있을까?
det.analysis:
✅ ④ undertook: 원문 그대로
✅ ② organized: 원문 그대로
✅ ③ input: 원문 그대로
❌ ① physical: 부적절 ← 정답
det.tip: legal rights(법적 권리) vs physical rights(물리적 권리). 저작권 논의에서는 legal이 맞음.

questions.passage: Artists usually sign their works of art to show authorship. A major concern related to authorship is the copyright of AI-generated art. Since current copyright law ①<u>applies</u> to humans, not machines, the "author" should be the person who arranged the creation. However, it is not always clear who undertook the ④<u>arrangements</u>. It could be the people who organized or ③<u>funded</u> the project, did the coding, or input a prompt. Could an AI machine itself ever be considered an author? It seems ②<u>inevitable</u>, but who knows how this question will be regarded in the future?

det.korean: 그것은 가능성이 낮아(unlikely) 보이지만, 이 질문이 미래에 어떻게 여겨질지 누가 알겠는가?
det.analysis:
✅ ① applies: 원문 그대로
✅ ④ arrangements: 원문 그대로
✅ ③ funded: 원문 그대로
❌ ② inevitable: 부적절 ← 정답
det.tip: unlikely(~할 것 같지 않은) ↔ inevitable(불가피한). 'It seems unlikely, but who knows' = 회의적이지만 열린 결론.

questions.passage:
Who Is the Author of AI-generated Art?

Artists usually sign their works of art to show authorship. But what about AI art? Who actually creates the work: the AI or the human using it? A major concern related to authorship is the copyright of AI-generated art. More and more companies, developers, and artists ask for legal protection of the artworks created by AI programs that they developed or used. Since current copyright law applies to humans, not machines, the "author" should be the person who ____. However, it is not always clear who undertook the arrangements. It could, for example, be the people who organized or funded the project, did the coding or "teaching" of the AI, or input a prompt.

Could an AI machine itself ever be considered an author with legal rights? It seems unlikely, but who knows how this question will be regarded in the future?

viewed the AI-generated artwork in a gallery

det.analysis: ✅ ①arranged the creation: 법적 저자 = 창작을 주선한 사람. ❌ ②purchased(구매): 구매자 ≠ 저자. ❌ ③viewed(관람): 관람자 ≠ 저자. ❌ ④criticized(비평): 비평가 ≠ 저자.
det.tip: arrange the creation = 창작을 주선/준비하다. 법적 저작자의 기준.
